description: Frame a charge under section 420 of the Penal Code 1871 (cheating and dishonestly inducing a delivery of property), or say why none can be framed
name: charge under s 420

f.description: The deception, what it induced, and the particulars of the charge

by remote communication.description: Was the cheating done by remote communication (s 420(2))?

cause the delivery.description: Was the victim induced to cause property to be delivered to anyone?

causes.description: Did that act or omission cause damage or harm?

consent that any person shall retain any.description: Was the victim induced to consent to anyone keeping property?

deceived the victim.description: Did the accused deceive the victim? A dishonest concealment of facts is a deception (Explanation 1); a representation made through an agent counts (Explanation 3); a company can be deceived (Explanation 4).

deliver.description: Was the victim induced to deliver property to anyone?

dishonestly.description: Did the accused act dishonestly — intending a wrongful gain or a wrongful loss, or in a way reasonable and honest people would call dishonest, knowing that (s 24)?

do.description: Was the victim induced to do something they would not have done but for the deception?

fraudulently.description: Did the accused act fraudulently — with intent to deceive, and by means of the deception, for an advantage to anyone or a detriment to anyone else (s 25)?

intentionally.description: Did the accused intend to induce the victim to act, or to refrain from acting, as they did?

likely to cause.description: Was that act or omission likely to cause damage or harm?

make, alter or destroy a valuable securi.description: Was the victim induced to make, alter or destroy the whole or any part of a valuable security, or anything signed or sealed that could be converted into one?

omit to do.description: Was the victim induced to leave undone something they would otherwise have done?

particulars.description: Who is charged, and when and where the offence was committed

accused.description: The accused person's full name, as it is to appear in the charge

co-accused.description: Anyone charged jointly with the accused, as they are to be named in the charge; leave blank if none

common intention.description: Was the act done in furtherance of a common intention shared with the co-accused, so that section 34 is read with the charge?

date.description: The date of the offence, as it is to read after "on or about" — for example "the 24th day of April 2000"

place.description: Where the offence was committed, as it is to read after "at" — "Singapore" is added for you

time.description: The time of day, as it is to read after "at about" — for example "8.10 pm"; leave blank if not known

the act or omission.description: What the victim did or left undone, as it is to read after "to" — for example "hand over the keys to the flat"

the deception.description: What the victim was deceived into, as it is to read after "by deceiving him/her" — for example "to believe that the price of a pencil casing is worth $5.25, when in actual fact, you knew that the price of the said item is worth $16.95"

the property.description: What was delivered or retained, as it is to read after "to deliver to you" — for example "the said item for only $5.25"

victim.description: The name of the person deceived, as it is to appear in the charge — for example "Wong Fei Hsia"

victim described as.description: How the charge describes the person deceived, after the name — for example "the cashier of Seiyu Departmental Store"; leave blank if not needed

victim pronoun.description: The pronoun the charge uses for the person deceived

propertyOrder: consent that any person shall retain any property
make, alter or destroy a valuable security
required: consent that any person shall retain any property
make, alter or destroy a valuable security

made out.description: Whether every legal condition of the offence is fulfilled on the facts given — a charge asserts that it is (CPC s 123(5))

offence.description: The name the Code gives the offence

punishment.description: The punishment the section prescribes, verbatim

refusal.description: Why no charge can be framed on these facts, or blank

section.description: The section of the Penal Code 1871 under which the charge is framed — the punishing section

text.description: The charge as it is to be read to the accused, or blank if it cannot be framed on these facts
